Look first · 3 min

Read the picture before the words

?!
Q1 · WHEREWhere are they? What kind of room is this? Find three clues.
A hotel manager's office: the key rack on the wall, the desk bell, the man with the moustache behind the desk.
Q2 · WHO & HOWWho is the man in the cap? How does he feel? How do you know?
A guest. Upset – his shoulders are down, his hands are open and empty, his eyes are down.
Q3 · WHATWhat do you think has happened? Start with: "I think he has…"
Open. Accept all ideas – write 2–3 on the board, then read to check.
Prediction first, reading second. Students who guess are students who read to check.

Teacher: 只用英文问答，不翻译。Q3 的答案板书 2–3 个，略读后回来打勾——猜对与否都算"读懂了"。

The title: It could be worse.

What it says – things are bad, but not as bad as they could be
A: I failed the test. B: It could be worse – you could have failed ALL of them.
When we say it – to comfort someone (or ourselves)
Chinese has the same idea: 不幸中之万幸. Today, what is the "bad"? And what is the "worse" that did NOT happen?
Click each line. Keep the question in mind while you read.

Teacher: 投票后随机请 2 位同学 30 秒分享。标题先解释用法，读完回到标题验证"坏事是什么、更坏的是什么没发生"。

Skim · 2 min

Read fast. Two questions, easy then hard.

2:00
Q1 · gistDid the writer get his $50 back? Who brought it?
Yes. A girl came in with an envelope containing $50 – she had found it outside his room.
Q2 · thinkThe manager said one thing about the world; the writer said the opposite. Find both lines.
Manager: "Everyone's losing money these days… this wicked world." Writer: "There is still some honesty in this world!" The girl's action proves the manager wrong.

Q1 信息题（谁、是否找回），Q2 对比题（两个人对"世界"的看法）。先看问题再按 Start；2 分钟后合上书回答。

Vocabulary

Eight words to take away

Say the Chinese first, then flip. Then close your eyes – your partner reads the Chinese, you say the English.

注意两个发音陷阱：wicked /ˈwɪkɪd/ 两个音节（形容词 -ed 读 /ɪd/，同 naked, crooked）；honesty 的 h 不发音。

Grammar focus

"I had just lost $50."

Two things in the past – which happened first? The earlier one takes had + past participle.

Build the timeline

NOW
had lost→ earlier →entered · sat down · felt
Click each event: is it the earlier past (red) or the story past (green)? The past perfect is only for the event that happened BEFORE the others – here, losing the money.

Which one comes first?

Teacher: 一句话总结——过去完成时不是"更早的过去"本身，而是"在另一个过去动作之前"。没有参照点就不用。最后一题是陷阱：顺序发生的动作用一般过去时。

Four lines, four moods. Click a line for the voice to use.

Wrap-up

Why "It could be worse"?

💬 Discuss (3 min)

"Well, there is still some honesty in this world!"
  • Back to the title: what was the bad thing? What worse thing did NOT happen?
  • The manager was "sympathetic, but he could do nothing". Was he really helpful? Is the writer's last line a little joke at him?
  • The girl could have kept the $50. Why didn't she? What would YOU do?

📝 Homework

  • Retell the story in 60–80 words from the girl's point of view ("I was cleaning the corridor when…").
  • Five sentences with the past perfect: When I …, … had already … / By the time …
  • Draw panel 5: what happens next? One picture + one speech bubble in English.

Exit ticket: 用 "It could be worse" 安慰同桌一句话（同桌先说一件小倒霉事）。

Look at the picture. What do you think it means? Guess in English!
